questions.q: In Tableau Next, what is a metric?
options: A measure combined with a time dimension, defined on a semantic model so it can be tracked over time
A page layout for record pages
A user permission
A screenshot of a dashboard
questions.explain: Metrics are built on semantic models and combine a measure with a time dimension so the KPI can be tracked as it changes.

questions.q: Which parts does the Tableau Next metric builder walk you through?
options: Import, Transform, and Export
Connect, Explore, and Share
Details, Value, and Insights
Create, Delete, and Archive
questions.explain: The metric wizard has Details (name and description), Value (measure, filter, time dimension, dimensions), and optional Insights.

questions.q: Which fields are required in the Value part of a metric?
options: A description and an owner
A measure and a time dimension
A filter and a dashboard
A workspace and a Slack channel
questions.explain: The measure and the time dimension are required; the filter and additional dimensions are optional.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call the description field a governance tool?
options: It changes the metric's calculation
It records what is included and excluded and who owns it, which prevents later disputes
It is required to be exactly ten characters
It hides the metric from other users
questions.explain: A good description states the definition, exclusions, and owner so people can find and trust the metric.

questions.q: A stakeholder wants a version of Closed Won Revenue that also includes open pipeline. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Quietly edit the original metric so everyone sees the new logic
Copy the calculation into a personal dashboard
Delete the original metric
Create a separate, clearly named metric rather than changing the original
questions.explain: Variants should be separate, clearly named metrics so the original definition stays stable and trustworthy.
